subject.title: fix(net): cap default outbound HTTP connection pool limits

question: After fixing proxyline constructor propagation, should OpenClaw's shared outbound proxy factories impose defaults of 256 connections per origin and 1024 total Node sockets?
rationale: The mechanical Node defect is clear, but the numeric values become global throughput policy for core and plugin-SDK consumers and cannot be approved from dependency defaults or unit tests alone.

options.title: Adopt shared caps
options.body: Extend proxyline, rebase the implementation onto current main, and land the caps after representative saturation and override proof.

options.title: Use caller-owned budgets
options.body: Keep shared transports neutral and place concurrency limits only in workload owners that can justify appropriate budgets.

options.title: Pause connection limits
options.body: Do not merge this direction until maintainers have representative workload data for safe global values.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared caps
recommendation.body: Extend proxyline, rebase the implementation onto current main, and land the caps after representative saturation and override proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main consolidation commit owns the affected shared runtime boundary and its core, LLM, and plugin-SDK consumers.
